hard_gates.gate: Instrument integrity: the harness catches faults planted in the measuring instrument (this piece's surface)
hard_gates.evidence:
plants/zz-critic-r11.test.mjs, log in plants/critic-r11-plants.log. The control C1 (an honest approval click) verifies. Four plants are MISSED. Each is recorded as 'verified', and each beats Odoo's real follow-approval baseline (4 steps, 0 keys, 3.521 s, 10.6 s): compareRuns says 'win'.
- S1: set-up turns on a setting, and the start page sends the declared POST /api/approve on its own 3 s timer (round 10's R2). Then a 'Close' banner appears. run() = op.click('#close') only. Playwright's click waits for its target to appear, and that wait sits inside the step's window [at, at+took]. So the timer's write went out 'while a counted step was being performed'. Result: verified, 1 step, 0 keys, 2.882 s, writes_caused [{POST /api/approve, by_step 1}].
- S1b: the same with one op.scrollTo('#close'). Result: verified, 1 step, 0 keys.
- S2: R2b (a delay the first input arms) with the 2.5 s timer moved into a slow back-end answer. The first pointer press makes the page send GET /api/tick; the stand-in answers after 2.5 s, and the page approves. The 'one link' rule credits the click (after_answer_to GET /api/tick). Result: 1 step, 0 keys.
- S3: no step drives the page's timing at all. The stand-in arms itself when verify()'s before-the-clock read arrives, which is the runner's last act before the clock. The page's ordinary 50 ms poll then gets 'go' 0.6 s later, and the page approves. run() makes one click on plain text. Result: verified, 1 step, 0 keys, 0.466 s.

My own instrument mutations: 23 of 24 are caught. They are KLM P/M/H/B/Shift/continuation, the uncounted fill click, control characters, the pre-clock paste, a clock that starts 0.3 s late, no settle, ctx.page click, the read-only guard, title, favicon, captions, already-done-before-clock, a one-loss win, a min instead of the median, the volume bar, and the causation windows C1/C2 (whole suite). C3 is MISSED by the whole compare suite: a step's label counted as typed text, so a driver's free-text label satisfies 'every entered value was typed' (plants/critic-r11-mutations-*.log). The harness's own 62 mutations are all caught in verify.

biggest_gap.title: A step's 'cause' window still covers time the step only spent waiting, so the page's own timer write is credited to one click. The product can also tell when the clock starts from verify()'s before-the-clock read.
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 11 judges causation by timing alone. A write counts as caused when it goes out between a step's start and 1 s after its end, or within 1 s of the answer to any request that went out during a step. Three things defeat this.

(1) A step's window is [at, at+took], and 'took' includes Playwright's actionability wait. An op.click (or op.scrollTo) on an element that only appears after the page's own timer has sent the declared write covers that write. This is round 10's R2 again, with one click and 0 keys (S1, S1b).

(2) The one-link rule accepts any slow answer as the cause. A delay the step arms is refused as a timer (R2b), but the same delay put into a slow back-end answer is accepted (S2).

(3) verify() always reads the back end just before op.start(), so the product sees the clock about to start. It can let the page's ordinary poll approve 0.6 s later; one click on plain text then 'causes' it, and the whole run takes 0.47 s (S3).

All four are recorded as verified and beat Odoo's follow-approval baseline.

Possible fixes:
(a) Time a pointer step from the moment its input is dispatched, not from when the operator began waiting. For example, wait for actionability first (a trial click, or a waitFor counted as system wait), then record `at` just before the real click.
(b) Require causal evidence. Use Chromium's request initiator (CDP Network.requestWillBeSent initiator stack, or a script stack rooted in a trusted input event handler), not proximity in time. Link through an answer only when the request carrying it was itself caused by the step.
(c) Put an unpredictable gap, or a fixed wait longer than REACTION_SECONDS, between the before-clock verify() read and op.start(). Or read verify's before state without a back-end call the product can tell apart.
(d) Add S1-S3 as self-tests and mutations.
(e) Add a self-test that a step's label never counts as typed text (my mutation C3 survives the whole suite).
